    StartersAndy's egg salad, bread includedEgg salad with Japanese mayo, Dijon and celery on breadHow to make it8 eggs100g Japanese mayonnaise2 tsp Dijon mustard1 celery stick1 bunch chives1 loaf soft milk bread50g butter, softened1 iceberg lettuceBoil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.Chop roughly and fold with the Japanese mayonnaise, the Dijon, the finely diced celery stick, the chives, salt and plenty of pepper.Butter the slices of soft milk bread.Lay iceberg lettuce on the slices, pile on the egg salad and close.Cut off the crusts, slice in half and press lightly.Smart Tech poker night queso dipChorizo queso and corn chips. Poker night, when the guys find outHow to make it1 chorizo sausage1 brown onion1 jalapeño1 tbsp cornflour375ml evaporated milk250g cheddar80g roasted red capsicumground cumin, to taste250g corn chips150g salted peanutsFry the diced chorizo until crisp.Add half a diced onion and the chopped jalapeño for 3 minutes.Stir in the cornflour, then the evaporated milk, and simmer until it thickens.Over low heat, stir in the grated cheddar a handful at a time until smooth, then the chopped roasted capsicum and a pinch of cumin.Serve hot in a pan with the corn chips and the salted peanuts.Hot lineTrish's lemon garlic roast chickenLemon roast chicken. Trish sells his collectibles to fund the storeHow to make it1.8kg whole chicken30g butter1 lemon1 head garlic1 bunch thyme1kg potatoes4 carrotsvegetable oil, to taste1 tbsp plain flour300ml chicken stockHeat the oven to 200°C.Rub the chicken with the soft butter, salt and pepper and stuff with the halved lemon, the garlic cloves and thyme.Toss the potatoes and the carrots in chunks with oil and salt around it.Roast 1 hour 15 minutes, turning the vegetables once.Rest the chicken 10 minutes.Whisk the flour into the pan juices, add the stock and simmer 3 minutes for gravy.Mooj's lamb rogan joshSlow-cooked lamb. Mooj says life is about passion and spiritHow to make it1kg lamb shoulder, diced200g Greek yoghurt2 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder2 brown onions4 garlic cloves20g ginger3 tbsp ghee1 tsp garam masala6 cardamom pods400g tinned crushed tomatoes300g basmati rice1 Lebanese cucumber1 bunch corianderFry the sliced onions in the ghee for 12 minutes until deep golden, then add the grated garlic and ginger, chilli, garam masala and cardamom for 1 minute.Add the lamb and brown on all sides, then stir in the tomatoes, 100g of the yoghurt and 250ml water.Cover and simmer gently for 1 and a half hours until the lamb is tender.Simmer the rice with 600ml water, covered, for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.Grate the cucumber, squeeze it out and mix with the rest of the yoghurt and a pinch of salt.Scatter the curry with coriander and serve with the rice and raita.SweetsSpeed dating salted chocolate trufflesSalted truffles. Andy and Trish wait until the 20th dateHow to make it120ml thickened cream200g dark chocolate20g buttercocoa powder, to taste40g hazelnutsfreeze-dried raspberries, to tastesea salt flakes, to tasteHeat the cream until just simmering and pour over the chopped dark chocolate.Stand 2 minutes, then stir until smooth with the butter and a pinch of salt.Chill 2 hours until firm.Scoop into balls and roll quickly in your hands.Roll a third in cocoa, a third in the crushed toasted hazelnuts and a third in crushed freeze-dried raspberries.Chill until serving.DrinksAndy's chocolate malt milkshakeThick chocolate malt. Andy bikes into a billboard truckHow to make it500g chocolate ice cream400ml milk3 tbsp malted milk powder100ml thickened cream60g chocolate malt ballsBlend the chocolate ice cream, the cold milk and the malted milk powder until thick and smooth.Pour into tall chilled glasses.Whip the cream to soft peaks and spoon on top.Crush the chocolate malt balls and scatter over.Serve with straws.
